citation_short: Huang Wang & Sun. Are long corolla tubes in Pedicularis driven by pollinator selection?
manipulation: P. tricolor corolla tube shortened by bending tube and fixing with clear sticky tape; P. siphonantha tube length varied under watering/shading
design_or_sample: P. tricolor: 12 flowering individuals; first arrivals to 72 shortened and 72 unmanipulated flowers; seed-set analysis F1,180. P. siphonantha: 25 plants in experimental plot plus 45 open-pollinated flowers.
response: bumblebee visitation; seed set; corolla tube length
key_result: P. tricolor visits/census shortened 2.70±0.34 vs control 2.61±0.37, P=0.857; seed set 0.45±0.022 vs 0.48±0.018, P=0.262
method_relevance: Strong congeneric non-destructive floral-dimension manipulation and sham/control feasibility precedent for P0.
notes: Supports manipulation family and off-target/visitor checks; does not validate realized exsertion manipulation in P. rex.

citation_short: Yang Sun & Guo. Resource limitation and pollen source affecting seed production in two louseworts
manipulation: Open pollination with supplemental self or outcross pollen; separate hand self/outcross pollination on bagged flowers
design_or_sample: Natural-population supplementation and bagged hand-pollination experiments; exact sample sizes not recovered from indexed abstract.
response: stigmatic pollen load; seed production per capsule; pollen limitation
key_result: Additional self/outcross pollen did not increase seed production in the open-pollination supplementation test; bagged hand self vs outcross treatments differed in seed production.
method_relevance: Direct congeneric precedent for adding self/outcross pollen and measuring seed-production response without inventing a new P1 treatment family.
notes: Method precedent only. Species differ from P. rex and reported lack of supplementation response is not a P. rex expected effect.

citation_short: Huang & Shi. Floral isolation in Pedicularis
target_stage: CAL_A; P1 method handling; exclusion/sham logic
manipulation: Galea gap or tip blocked with glue; open pollination or pollinator exclusion by small nylon nets
design_or_sample: 10 plants per species; on each plant three flowers assigned to gap-blocked/open, tip-blocked/open, or tip-blocked/bagged; pilot tested glue brands and found manipulated flowers were not discriminated by bumblebees.
response: pollen grains remaining at gap/tip; bee-body pollen placement; stigma contact
key_result: Tip-blocked open flowers retained far more tip pollen than pollinator-excluded flowers in all eight species (all P<0.001); manipulation pilot reported no bumblebee discrimination.
method_relevance: Strong Pedicularis precedent for flower-level handling controls, physical blocking, bagging/exclusion and explicit visitor-discrimination checks.
notes: Not a pollen-supplementation effect and not seed-predator exclusion; useful method-control precedent only.

citation_short: Sun & Huang. Rainwater in cupulate bracts repels seed herbivores
manipulation: Bract water drained vs intact control; visitor censuses and seed outcomes
design_or_sample: Six populations; 40-60 tagged individuals/population; 20-30 drained individuals/population; >=6 capsules/individual; Shama visitor plots included five drained and five intact plots.
response: pollinator and nectar-robber visitation; initial/final seed set; seed predation
key_result: Drainage changed seed predation/final seed outcome while no detected treatment effect occurred for pollinator visit rate or initial seed set.
method_relevance: Same-species precedent for testing antagonist-related intervention selectivity and measuring contamination endpoints.
notes: Water drainage remains deprecated as SCH independent G. It supports handling/selectivity logic and BITA-y, not the current predator-exclusion intervention.

citation_short: Dai Kadiori Wang & Yang. Pollen limitation plasticity and mixed mating in Pedicularis siphonantha
manipulation: Supplemental hand pollination with outcross pollen across four large populations from 3200-4300 m
design_or_sample: Four large populations; exact within-plant allocation is not taken from the indexed abstract.
response: seed production per capsule; fruit set; pollen limitation; floral traits
key_result: Outcross supplementation significantly increased seed production per capsule in high-altitude populations but not lower-altitude populations.
method_relevance: Congeneric evidence that P1 supplementation effects can be strongly context-dependent across populations.
notes: Effect-heterogeneity precedent. Do not attach the 20-individual/three-flower design to this DOI unless verified from this paper's own full text.

citation_short: Dai Amboka Kadiori Wang & Yang. Phenotypic plasticity of floral traits and pollination adaption in transplanted Pedicularis siphonantha
manipulation: Within-individual natural vs supplemental self vs supplemental outcross pollen treatment
design_or_sample: Three natural plus two transplanted populations; 20 randomly selected individuals per population; three marked flowers per individual, assigned to self supplement, outcross supplement, or open control.
response: seed production per capsule; PL_S and PL_X pollen-limitation indices
key_result: PL_S=(F_IS-F_IN)/F_IN and PL_X=(F_IX-F_IN)/F_IN; flowers harvested at fruit maturity for seed count.
method_relevance: Very direct congeneric paired-within-plant P1 protocol precedent matching the intended SCH design structure.
notes: Protocol-detail precedent from Journal of Mountain Science 14(10):1995-2002; keep distinct from the separate 2017 JSE altitude paper.

citation_short: Sun Liao Xia & Guo. Floral colour change in Pedicularis monbeigiana
manipulation: Open control; bagging; bagged hand geitonogamy; supplemental outcross pollen from plants about 30 m away
design_or_sample: Control n=20 plants; bagged n=12; bagged hand-geitonogamy n=12; supplemental outcross n=12. Three field sites also had >20 open-pollinated plants each.
response: seed set; fruit set; mating-system response
key_result: Supplemental outcross seed set was not statistically different from open control, whereas hand geitonogamy significantly reduced seed production. Open-site fruit set was 94.7±3.2%, 96.2±3.0%, 94.2±4.3%; open-site seed set 41.7±9.3%, 38.2±8.4%, 37.6±9.0% (N>20/site).
method_relevance: Congeneric P1 precedent with explicit open/supplement/bagging/geitonogamy arms and exact treatment sample sizes.
notes: Useful for treatment family, handling controls and the possibility of a true near-zero supplementation effect under adequate natural pollination; reported ± label for site summaries is retained without assuming SD vs SE.

citation_short: Liao et al. Co-flowering species facilitates reproductive success of Pedicularis monbeigiana
manipulation: Whole-plant supplemental outcross pollination versus natural control repeated every two days through anthesis
design_or_sample: Within each experimental plot, 10 Pedicularis plants were hand-supplemented and 10 were controls; another eight plots were manipulated in population V in 2010. Pollen was pooled from 20 flowers on five non-focal donors about 100 m away.
response: fruit set per plant; seed set per fruit; pollen deposition
key_result: Treatment effect: fruit set F1,304=107.12, P≤0.001; seed set F1,304=113.27, P≤0.001. Supplemental seed set relative to control was 2.1× and 1.1× in pure sparse/dense plots, and +36% and +35% in mixed sparse/dense plots. Plot-type×treatment interaction seed set F=18.13, P≤0.001.
method_relevance: Strong congeneric whole-plant supplementation precedent that explicitly avoids flower-level resource-reallocation bias and demonstrates large context-dependent P1 effects.
notes: Alternative P1 design precedent: repeated whole-plant supplementation can estimate pollen limitation with less within-plant resource reallocation than a single supplemented flower. Effect magnitudes are not P. rex priors without explicit external-scenario labeling.

citation_short: Menges Waller & Gawler. Seed Set and Seed Predation in Pedicularis furbishiae
manipulation: Aluminum-mesh cages over elongating immature scapes to exclude spittlebugs; cages removed before flowers opened to allow pollination
design_or_sample: Mesh cages 1.5 m tall and 2 m2 over groups of 3-6 immature scapes; later comparison included N=45 spittlebug-present vs N=21 spittlebug-excluded inflorescences.
response: flower/capsule production; later lepidopteran seed predation
key_result: Pre-flowering mesh exclusion did not reduce later lepidopteran predation; authors note mesh-covered scapes had the same predation level as other plants, indicating Amblyptilia attack occurred after pollination.
method_relevance: Pedicularis-genus timing precedent showing that an intervention removed before flowering does not exclude later seed predators; supports post-pollination timing logic but is not a validated P. rex predator-exclusion method.
notes: Negative-control timing precedent only. Target herbivore in the mesh experiment was spittlebugs, not the seed predator; do not relabel as successful independent G.
